journal_name: International Journal of Software Engineering and Knowledge Engineering

abstracts.abstract: This paper presents a novel knowledge-graph-based theoretical framework for understanding and predicting software architecture evolution. Traditional software architecture research has predominantly relied on static modeling approaches that inadequately capture the dynamic nature of system growth and the interdependencies among architectural components. We propose a paradigm shift by conceptualizing software architecture as a living knowledge network where design decisions, code artifacts, and evolutionary patterns are represented as interconnected knowledge entities. Our framework introduces semantic proximity measures that capture both syntactic and semantic relationships between architectural elements, enabling more accurate prediction of architectural decay and maintenance challenges. We validate the theoretical foundations through formal reasoning and empirical analysis of 47 open-source software systems spanning diverse domains. The results demonstrate that our knowledge-centric approach provides superior explanatory power for architectural evolution phenomena compared to conventional metrics-based models. This work contributes to both software engineering and knowledge engineering by bridging the gap between architectural knowledge representation and evolutionary dynamics, opening new avenues for AI-driven architecture management.

Accurate measurement of software quality remains a fundamental challenge in software engineering practice. This paper presents an enhanced theoretical model for multi-dimensional software quality assessment that significantly extends the established ISO/IEC 25010 standard. While existing approaches treat quality characteristics as independent factors, our improved model incorporates interaction effects and contextual dependencies among quality attributes. We introduce novel theoretical constructs including quality attribute synergy coefficients and contextual adjustment factors that capture project-specific characteristics affecting quality interpretation. The formal foundations of our model are established through rigorous mathematical derivation based on multi-criteria decision analysis and fuzzy logic theory. Evaluation conducted across 128 software projects from industrial settings demonstrates that our enhanced model achieves 23% higher predictive accuracy for post-release defect density compared to state-of-the-art approaches. Furthermore, the proposed quality interaction framework provides actionable insights for software teams seeking to optimize resource allocation across quality improvement activities. This contribution advances software metrics theory by providing a more nuanced and practically applicable framework for quality assessment.

This paper introduces ARCHIMEDES, a novel knowledge-driven system for AI-augmented software architecture design that fundamentally reimagines the role of artificial intelligence in software development processes. Unlike existing tools that focus on code generation or bug detection, ARCHIMEDES implements an architectural co-creation paradigm where AI systems and human architects engage in collaborative knowledge construction. The system comprises three core components: a knowledge base of architectural patterns and design rationales, a reasoning engine employing deep learning for pattern recommendation, and an interactive visualization module supporting design space exploration. Our architectural knowledge representation scheme extends traditional ADL notations with semantic annotations enabling inference and recommendation capabilities. We conducted a controlled experiment with 32 professional software architects using ARCHIMEDES for designing enterprise-scale systems. The results reveal a 41% reduction in design time and a 35% improvement in architectural quality scores compared to conventional approaches. The system demonstrates particular effectiveness in identifying non-obvious pattern combinations and anticipating long-term maintainability implications. This work establishes a new paradigm for AI integration in software engineering, positioning AI as a collaborative knowledge partner rather than a mere automation tool.

Software maintenance constitutes a substantial portion of software lifecycle costs, yet automated refactoring support remains limited in practical tooling. This paper presents REFACTORFLOW, an enhanced refactoring automation system that significantly improves upon existing approaches by integrating machine learning with knowledge-based recommendation. The system addresses key limitations of prior work, including lack of contextual awareness and poor handling of cross-cutting concerns. REFACTORFLOW implements a multi-phase architecture comprising code smell detection using improved ensemble classifiers, knowledge-aware recommendation generation drawing from a curated repository of refactoring patterns, and automated refactoring execution with comprehensive change impact analysis. We substantially improved the underlying detection accuracy by incorporating graph neural networks for learning structural code patterns, achieving 18% higher precision than the previous state-of-the-art. The knowledge base incorporates 156 refined refactoring patterns organized by architectural layer and quality attribute impact. Evaluation using 23 real-world software systems demonstrates that REFACTORFLOW correctly identifies and safely executes refactoring operations with 94% success rate, reducing manual effort by an average of 67%. The system has been integrated into popular IDE platforms and is freely available for research purposes.
